title: Add wt config diff command
description:
Add diff command to show configuration differences.

## Proposed command
```bash
wt config diff
# Shows differences between actual config and defaults

wt config diff --local
# Shows local vs global config differences (after wt-j62)
```

## Requirements
1. Show which keys differ from defaults
2. Show added/removed hooks
3. Support --local flag (after wt-j62) for local vs global diff
4. Clear output format showing old vs new values

## Example output
```
$ wt config diff
worktree.location: dedicated (default) → per-repo
worktree.dedicated_path: ~/worktrees (default) → /tmp/wt
tmux.attach_on_create: true (default) → false

+ hooks.on_worktree_create:
  - run: "npm install"
    background: true
```

## Dependencies
- wt-979 (wt config command) - must be completed first
- wt-j62 (--local flag) - for local vs global diff

title: Implement wt config command (get, set, unset, list, validate)
description:
Implement programmatic config manipulation to avoid manual YAML editing.

## Design document
docs/plans/2026-01-26-wt-config-command-design.md

## Implementation plan
docs/plans/2026-01-26-wt-config-command-implementation.md

## Subcommands to implement (5 total)
- `wt config get <key>` - Retrieve scalar value using dot-notation
- `wt config set <key> <value>` - Set scalar value (global config only)
- `wt config unset <key>` - Remove key from config
- `wt config list` - Dump full config YAML to stdout
- `wt config validate` - Check YAML syntax + schema validity

3. Phase 3: CLI subcommands (5 commands)

title: Refactor project-local config from .wt.yaml to .wt/config.yaml
description:
Move project-local configuration from .wt.yaml to .wt/config.yaml for better organization and XDG compliance.

## Current state
- Config discovery order: --config flag → .wt.yaml → ~/.config/wt/config.yaml
- Project config is a single file in repo root

## Proposed change
- Use .wt/config.yaml directory instead of .wt.yaml file
- Allows future expansion (.wt/config.yaml, .wt/hooks/, .wt/state/)
- More explicit configuration directory
- Better separation from repo root

## Changes required
1. Update FindConfig() to look for .wt/config.yaml
2. Add migration path (check .wt.yaml, suggest rename)
3. Update documentation
4. Consider deprecation warning for .wt.yaml

## Related
- Config discovery: internal/config/config.go:133
- Config doc: docs/usage.md:162

title: wt remove: add --delete-branch flag
description:
Add a --delete-branch flag to wt remove that also deletes the associated git branch when removing a worktree.

Currently, wt remove only deletes the worktree directory and unregisters it from git, but leaves the branch intact. This feature would allow cleanup of both the worktree AND its branch in one command.

Example:
  wt remove /path/to/worktree --delete-branch

This would:
1. Remove the worktree (existing behavior)
2. Delete the associated git branch (new behavior)

The flag should:
- Work with --force flag (delete branch even if worktree has uncommitted changes)
- Only delete branches that are not checked out anywhere else
- Error gracefully if branch cannot be deleted (protected, checked out elsewhere, etc.)
- Support dry-run preview (print which branch would be deleted)
close_reason: Worktree location unification complete. All commands now use worktree.location config. global.worktree_root removed.

title: Add --local flag support to wt config set/unset
description:
Add --local flag to wt config set/unset commands for project-local config manipulation.

## Current state
- wt config set/unset only write to global (~/.config/wt/config.yaml)
- No way to modify .wt.yaml via CLI

## Proposed change
Add --local flag:
```bash
wt config set --local worktree.location dedicated
# Writes to .wt.yaml (or .wt/config.yaml after wt-cvr)

wt config set --global worktree.location per-repo
# Explicitly write to ~/.config/wt/config.yaml (default)
```

## Requirements
1. Add --local and --global flags to set/unset commands
2. --local writes to .wt.yaml in current directory
3. Default remains global (backwards compatible)
4. Update help text to indicate scope

## Dependencies
- wt-979 (wt config command) must be completed first
- wt-cvr (config path refactor) - wait for this or support both paths

## Design reference

title: Add wt config hook manipulation commands
description:
Add commands to manage hooks programmatically instead of editing YAML.

## Proposed commands
```bash
wt config add-hook on_worktree_create "npm install"
wt config remove-hook on_worktree_create 0
wt config list-hooks on_worktree_create
```

## Requirements
1. add-hook: Append hook to hook array
2. remove-hook: Remove hook by index (show list first)
3. list-hooks: Display hooks with indices
4. Support both on_worktree_create and on_worktree_remove

## Design questions
- Should add-hook support all hook options (cwd, background, parallel)?
- How to handle duplicate hook commands?
- Global vs local scope (--local flag from wt-j62)?

## Dependencies
- wt-979 (wt config command) - must be completed first
- wt-j62 (--local flag) - useful for per-project hooks
